description: Helium by viznut, a 3,761-byte intro with AdLib music that won the PC 4K intro competition at Assembly '97, running from its original files in your browser.
about: Helium is viznut's 4K intro for MS-DOS, a short story told in 3,761 bytes with AdLib music, which won the PC 4K intro competition at Assembly '97, held from 8 to 10 August 1997 in Helsinki.

viznut's notes on it say the competition's rules did not allow music at the time; HELIUM.TXT says its sound was “not included in the compo version”. The same file credits Lithium by Vista for its name, its explosions and its “sucking palettes”.
It returns to DOS by itself after about a minute and a half; Escape ends it sooner.
released: Assembly '97: first of 8 in the PC 4K intro competition, with 1,748 points.
terms: None in its own files. viznut's source package, helisrc.zip, says “It's yours. Use it any way you like.” (HELISRC.NFO), and since 2021 his repository github.com/viznut/demoscene has put Helium's source and its 3,756-byte build under CC0 1.0. That build is the one in helisrc.zip; this archive holds the 3,761-byte build of 5 August 1997, which the grant covers only as an earlier build of the same code.
accuracy: It draws in a tweaked VGA mode of 256 lines, which DosKit shows as it is: at 4:3 it would be stretched about 35% wider.
Its AdLib music plays through the FM chip of the emulated Sound Blaster 16.
Not yet compared with a capture made on real hardware.
